verification.note: Confirmed by reading the code; nothing was run. upload.py:132-133 refuses any existing path. upload.py:222-231 checks only size, and upload.py:246-247 finishes a subtitle with no content check and no row. files.py:1358 calls read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig") unguarded, and backend/app has no exception_handler, so a Shift_JIS file with Japanese text should give a 500. useShellCaptions.ts:39-51 and VideoPlayer.tsx:240-259 offer the generated track only when no sidecar is listed; useShellCaptions.ts:68 and :78 turn the failure into empty cues and `unavailable`. delete_folder (fileops.py:930-944) only soft-deletes rows and removes no sidecar, and renaming or moving the video carries the sidecar along (subtitle.py:106-139), so neither removes it. One limit on the claim: the bad file cannot be corrected or removed, but the user can upload a good file under another track name, such as movie.ja.srt, and pick it. The generated track stays hidden and a bare bad file still sorts first (subtitle.py:102). The unguarded read is older than this change per r5/triage.md:150; the dead end comes from 57dcc7303 together with the removal of the row and card. The docs and test greps match the finding.

Confirmed by reading the code; nothing was run. It has the same root as the claude-read finding. upload.py:132-133, :222-231 and :246-247, files.py:1354-1358 and useShellCaptions.ts:38-51, :67-69 and :78 all say what is claimed, and VideoPlayer.tsx:250-259 hides the generated track in the same way. known-issues.md:265-269 records that the file cannot be replaced or removed, but not the false success or the lost generated track. Earlier escape routes are supported by decisions.md:33, which records a card for an uploaded .srt, decisions.md:37, where purge removed the file from disk, and r5/triage.md:148-149, which records that replacement was possible in r5. The seventh R-5 run at decisions.md:78-80 used readable text. The claim of no in-app way to fix or remove the file holds for that file, with one limit: a differently named track can still be uploaded and selected.

Confirmed by reading the tests against upload.py:132-133, a single unconditional check; mutations were reasoned through, not run. test_upload.py:97-106 asserts a 409 for an existing .txt, and test_sidecar_subtitles_follow_video.py:358-371 asserts a 409 in a subfolder for a subtitle. Removing the check, restricting it to subtitles, exempting subtitles, or ignoring folder_path is each killed by at least one of those two tests, so none needs test_an_existing_file_of_another_type_still_refuses_the_upload (lines 373-383). Only a contrived mutation that special-cases .md would be killed by this test alone. testing-and-comments.md:37-38 says such a test is deleted or folded into the test that holds the property.

specification_compliance: known-issues.md:265-269 documents that an uploaded subtitle cannot be replaced or removed from the UI, but not the case where the file landed unreadable or the hidden generated track.
The refusal in upload.py:132-133 matches the 409 documented in known-issues.md and the seventh R-5 run at decisions.md:79.
potential_unspecified_behavior: A non-UTF-8 subtitle upload completes with a 200 and a sidecar answer, while the serving route's read at files.py:1358 has no guard against a decode error.

A subtitle over 5 MB also lands with a success answer and is then refused with a 413 by files.py:1355-1356, leaving the same dead end. Both players still list it, so it also hides the generated track.
regression_risks: If the serving route starts decoding more encodings, the 500 goes away, but a wrongly decoded file would still have no in-app way to be replaced or removed.
Deleting the duplicate test loses no mutation kill by this analysis, provided test_duplicate_filename stays.
test_coverage: No test named for subtitles uploads or serves a non-UTF-8 subtitle. The encoding-related matches in test_subtitle.py and test_sidecar_subtitles_follow_video.py are all encoding="utf-8" writes.
No test in those two files covers an oversized uploaded subtitle was not established by search; only encoding terms were searched.
test_an_existing_file_of_another_type_still_refuses_the_upload overlaps test_duplicate_filename and the second-upload refusal test.
